tasks.behavior: A rate bucket that does not refill holds on every CPU, and the cross-chain tracking tests pass on Linux
acceptance: On amd64, as on arm64, an empty rate bucket that does not refill makes a request wait instead of letting it through.

notes: 2026-11-11 review pass by subagent: Normal rates are unchanged; the new branch needs rate <= 0 or a wait past MaxInt64, where the old conversion was CPU-dependent (MaxInt64 on arm64, MinInt64 on amd64). Every Buckets.Wait caller only checks wait > 0 or ceils it into Retry-After (9223372037 at the max, fits int). Production rates are all positive; rate 0 occurs only in the cross-chain budget test. The new mid test can only fail on x86, so the staging run is its proof. No other exact next-check comparison in the cross-chain tests uses an untruncated time.Now().

proof.1: backend-affected: TestAnEmptyBucketThatDoesNotRefillWaitsOnEveryCPU checks that a bucket with rate 0 or 1e-12 waits the longest once empty. The httpapi tests pass.
proof.2: backend-affected: the tracking tests now truncate their start times to microseconds; with 123 ns added to the start and no truncation, TestWorkerFollowsAQuoteFromDepositToConversion failed here with the CI message 'waiting: next ...', and passed once truncated. The httpapi tests pass twice with -race.
